about: Bowed before the middle of the altar, the priest says this prayer quietly. He asks the Holy Trinity to accept his service and sacrifice and, in mercy, to make it propitiatory for him and for all those for whom it was offered.

s01.narrative: Then the celebrant bows before the middle of the altar, joins his hands upon it, and says silently:

s02.translation: Holy Trinity, may this act of my service please You. Grant that the sacrifice which I, though unworthy, have offered before Your majesty may be acceptable to You and, through Your mercy, propitiatory for me and for all for whom I offered it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

w001.explanation: What is to please God is “obséquium” (w005), the homage offered, not the priest himself.

w013.note: The form is dative and ablative plural at once. Nothing in the sentence decides whether the sacrifice is offered TO the eyes of Thy majesty or BEFORE them. This edition takes the dative and marks the doubt.

w016.explanation: “Indígnus” describes the priest who offers: “I, unworthy, have offered”.

w029.explanation: With “miseránte” (w030) it forms an ablative absolute, which English turns into a clause: “Thou showing mercy”, that is, through Thy mercy.
